name: Hatebreed
label: Victory
lede: A Connecticut hardcore band cut a Victory debut that sold 158,000 copies, then took the breakdown to Ozzfest and the Grammys, and got a video banned by MTV that its own singer later played as host of Headbangers Ball.

eras.title: New Haven, and a new band by the debut
eras.text: Hatebreed came out of the New Haven and Bridgeport hardcore scene in 1994. Half the founders were gone before the first album, and the version that made Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire turned a Victory Records debut into the label's best seller of its kind.

years.h: Jamey Jasta and Chris Beattie start Hatebreed in Connecticut
years.p: The first Hatebreed: Jasta singing, Beattie on bass, Wayne Lozinak and Larry Dwyer Jr. on guitars, Dave Russo on drums.

years.h: Under the Knife EP: stuck at one label, released by the band
years.p: Hatebreed's first EP was due out on Big Wheel Recreation in 1995. When that didn't happen, the band put it out themselves in 1996.

years.h: Wayne Lozinak, Larry Dwyer Jr. and Dave Russo leave Hatebreed
years.p: Three of Hatebreed's five founders are gone by the end of 1996. Nick Papantoniou drums for 1996–97; Lozinak won't be back until 2009.

years.cap: Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire, Victory, 1997
years.h: Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire on Victory Records
years.p: Jasta and Beattie with a nearly all-new line-up, including guitarist Lou Richards. According to Wikipedia, it sold 158,000 copies, Victory's best-selling debut.

eras.title: Banned on MTV, then hosting it
eras.text: Hatebreed left Victory for Universal, and its hardcore breakdowns ended up at Ozzfest and in Hollywood soundtracks. By 2003 Jamey Jasta was the face of MTV2's metal show, and in 2005 the band was at the Grammys.

years.h: Hatebreed plays its first Ozzfest
years.p: The first of four Ozzfest summers for Hatebreed (2001, 2002, 2006, 2007).

years.h: MTV bans Hatebreed's I Will Be Heard video
years.p: The video, directed by Marc Webb, is initially banned from MTV, then gets played on MTV2's Headbangers Ball. The song also lands on the soundtrack to the Vin Diesel film XXX.

years.h: Matt Byrne takes over Hatebreed's drums mid-album
years.p: Byrne replaces Rigg Ross partway through the recording of Perseverance, and is still Hatebreed's drummer a quarter century later.

years.h: Perseverance, Hatebreed's Universal debut
years.p: Produced by Matt Hyde at Long View Farm in North Brookfield, Massachusetts, with Sean Martin on lead guitar. It debuts at No. 50 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Guitarist Lou Richards leaves Hatebreed
years.p: Lou "Boulder" Richards, who played on Satisfaction and Perseverance, departs after the second album.

years.h: Jamey Jasta becomes host of MTV2's Headbangers Ball
years.p: Hatebreed's singer fronts the revived metal show, and uses it to get airtime for videos MTV had banned.

years.h: The Rise of Brutality debuts at No. 30
years.p: Hatebreed's third album sells 32,515 copies in its first week, per Wikipedia. Below the Bottom goes on the soundtrack of the 2003 Texas Chainsaw Massacre remake.

years.h: Hatebreed's Live for This is nominated for a Grammy
years.p: The song is up for Best Metal Performance at the 47th Grammy Awards. [[Motörhead|57961a97-3796-4bf7-9f02-a985a8979ae9]] wins.

eras.title: Roadrunner, and losing Boulder
eras.text: Hatebreed moved to Roadrunner and kept climbing the charts. The same year, the guitarist who played on its first two albums died, and by 2009 a founding member was back.

years.h: Supremacy, Hatebreed's Roadrunner debut
years.p: Hatebreed's fourth album, its first on Roadrunner Records, debuts at No. 31 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Frank Novinec joins Hatebreed on guitar
years.p: Novinec comes in in 2006 and stays through the next two decades of line-up changes.

years.h: Former Hatebreed guitarist Lou Richards dies at 35
years.p: Richards, who played on Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire and Perseverance, died by suicide, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Sean Martin leaves; founder Wayne Lozinak returns
years.p: Martin exits in February 2009 and Lozinak, gone since 1996, comes back on guitar.

years.h: For the Lions and Hatebreed, two albums on Koch
years.p: Hatebreed puts out a covers album, For the Lions, and a self-titled album of originals in the same year, both on Koch Records.

eras.title: The veterans' chart peak
eras.text: Twenty years in, Hatebreed hit its highest chart position and kept an album-every-few-years pace, with the Byrne, Novinec, Lozinak and Beattie line-up behind Jasta.

years.h: The Divinity of Purpose: Hatebreed's highest chart peak
years.p: Hatebreed's sixth album of originals reaches No. 20 on the Billboard 200, the band's best showing.

years.h: The Concrete Confessional
years.p: Hatebreed's seventh studio album.

years.h: Weight of the False Self, Hatebreed's eighth album
years.p: The last album with founding bassist Chris Beattie in the band.

eras.title: An anniversary, a firing and a lawsuit
eras.text: Hatebreed celebrated Perseverance with an old member back on stage, then fired the last founder besides Jasta. The fight went to court, and a health scare took a guitarist off the road.

years.h: Sean Martin rejoins for the Perseverance 20th anniversary tour
years.p: Hatebreed brings back the guitarist from the 2002 album for its anniversary run.

years.h: Hatebreed fires founding bassist Chris Beattie
years.p: Beattie, in Hatebreed since 1994, says the split was not his decision. In July 2025 he sued Jamey Jasta, claiming Jasta's increasingly erratic behavior led to Beattie being cut off from his career.
years.xp:
The suit leans on a 2015 merchandise agreement that, according to Wikipedia's summary, gave Beattie, Jasta and Matt Byrne 25 percent each of merch revenue, with the other members at 12.5 percent. Hatebreed's side called Beattie a disgruntled former member in an at-will arrangement, and said the agreement gave him no rights to the Hatebreed name.

Matt Bachand has filled in on bass on tour since 2025.

years.h: Wayne Lozinak leaves a European tour with a brain tumor
years.p: Lozinak steps away from Hatebreed's 2025 European dates after a brain tumor diagnosis, and has successful surgery in August 2025.

years.h: Hatebreed's ninth album is slated for fall 2026
years.p: According to Wikipedia, the next Hatebreed album is due in fall 2026 through BLKIIBLK Records.
